title: AASI for Sleep Apnea/Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA)

blocks.text: AMEs may re-issue an airman medical certificate to airmen currently on an AASI for OSA if the individual provides the following:
blocks.html: AMEs may re-issue an airman medical certificate to airmen currently on an AASI for OSA if the individual provides the following:

blocks.text:
- An Authorization granted by the FAA; AND
- A completed and signed OSA TREATED STATUS REPORT
blocks.html:
• An Authorization granted by the FAA; AND
  • A completed and signed OSA TREATED STATUS REPORT

blocks.text: - A current Detailed Clinical Progress Note from your treating physician indicating that OSA treatment is still effective AND - For CPAP/ BIPAP/ APAP: - A copy of the cumulative annual PAP device report which shows actual time used (rather than a report typically generated for insurance providers which only shows if use is greater or less than 4 hours). Target goal should show use for at least 75% of sleep periods and an average minimum of 6 hours use per sleep period.
blocks.html:
• • A

    current Detailed Clinical Progress Note

    from your treating physician indicating that OSA treatment is still effective AND

    • o For CPAP/ BIPAP/ APAP:

      • A copy of the cumulative annual PAP device report which shows actual time used (rather than a report typically generated for insurance providers which only shows if use is greater or less than 4 hours). Target goal should show use for at least 75% of sleep periods and an average minimum of 6 hours use per sleep period.

blocks.text: - - - For persons with an established diagnosis of OSA who do not have a recording CPAP, a one-year exception will be allowed to provide a personal statement that they regularly use CPAP and use it before each shift when performing flight or safety duties.
blocks.html: • For persons with an established diagnosis of OSA who do not have a recording CPAP, a one-year exception will be allowed to provide a personal statement that they regularly use CPAP and use it before each shift when performing flight or safety duties.

blocks.text: - - For Dental Devices and/or for Positional Devices:
blocks.html: • o For Dental Devices and/or for Positional Devices:

blocks.text: No conditions known to be co-morbid with OSA (e.g., diabetes mellitus, hypertension treated with more than two medications, atrial fibrillation, etc). Once Dental Devices with recording / monitoring capability are available, reports must be submitted.
blocks.html: No conditions known to be co-morbid with OSA (e.g., diabetes mellitus, hypertension treated with more than two medications, atrial fibrillation, etc). Once Dental Devices with recording / monitoring capability are available, reports must be submitted.

blocks.text: For successfully treated surgical patients, a statement attesting to the continued absence of OSA symptoms is required.
blocks.html: For successfully treated surgical patients, a statement attesting to the continued absence of OSA symptoms is required.

blocks.text: Defer to the AMCD or the Region for further review if:
blocks.html: Defer to the AMCD or the Region for further review if:

blocks.text:
- Concerns about adequacy of therapy or non-compliance;
- Significant weight gain or development of conditions known to be co-morbid with OSA (e.g., diabetes mellitus, hypertension treated with more than two medications, atrial fibrillation, etc).
blocks.html:
• Concerns about adequacy of therapy or non-compliance;
  • Significant weight gain or development of conditions known to be co-morbid with OSA (e.g., diabetes mellitus, hypertension treated with more than two medications, atrial fibrillation, etc).

blocks.text: Note: The AME may request AMCD review to discontinue the AASI if there are indications that the airman no longer has OSA (e.g., significant weight loss and a negative study or surgical intervention followed by 3 years of symptom abatement and absence of significant weight gain or co-morbid conditions). In most cases, a follow-up sleep study will be required to remove the AASI.
